title: Variables (Part 1) - Mutable bindings
learning_objectives: Distinguish Rust's default immutable bindings from mutable ones.
Add `mut` when a binding must change over time.
Interpret compiler feedback for invalid reassignment.
explanation: This slice focuses on one core rule: bindings are immutable by default. When a value needs to change, mark the binding with `mut` so the compiler knows reassignment is intentional.

examples.title: Immutable bindings reject reassignment
Mutable bindings allow counters to change

compiler_error_examples: error[E0384]: cannot assign twice to immutable variable
completion_criteria: Exercise tests pass for incrementing a mutable counter
Learner can explain why the binding, not just the value, must be mutable
